_comment: All projects derive from the CV. To add a project, append an object. Each links to a related publication id where applicable. Add image/code/video paths when available; empty strings render a placeholder or hide the action.

projects.title: Learned Differential Inverse Kinematics for Non-Spherical Wrist Manipulators
projects.tagline: Zero-shot sim-to-real trajectory tracking via reinforcement learning
projects.overview: A reinforcement-learning controller that performs continuous, accurate end-effector trajectory tracking on manipulators whose wrist geometry breaks the assumptions behind closed-form inverse kinematics.
projects.problem: Non-spherical wrist manipulators exhibit kinematic coupling and joint-space discontinuities that make analytical inverse kinematics ill-conditioned, producing jerky or infeasible motion near singular configurations.
projects.motivation: Many low-cost collaborative arms used in research and industry do not satisfy the spherical-wrist condition, yet smooth trajectory tracking is a prerequisite for manipulation, assembly and tele-operation. A learned controller that generalises across the workspace removes the need for per-robot analytical derivations.
projects.methodology: A Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) policy is trained in NVIDIA Isaac Lab over 1.5 million reachable poses. The policy maps a 25-dimensional pose-error vector directly to joint velocities, optimising a custom reward that balances tracking accuracy against energy efficiency.
projects.technical: Massively parallel simulation in Isaac Lab; 25-D observation of pose error; continuous joint-velocity action space; reward shaping for accuracy and effort; domain considerations enabling transfer.
projects.results: The policy achieves zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on a physical Kinova Gen3 Lite, tracking continuous trajectories at 20 Hz without any real-world fine-tuning.
projects.future: Extension to dynamic obstacle fields, payload variation, and dual-arm coordinated tracking; integration with task-level planners for full manipulation pipelines.

projects.title: Competitive Task Allocation with Real-Time Collision Avoidance for Dual-Arm Manipulation
projects.tagline: Spatially and temporally aware coordination for cooperating arms
projects.overview: A proximity-based competitive task-allocation framework that lets two arms decide, in real time, which arm services which target while guaranteeing inter-arm safety.
projects.problem: When two manipulators share a workspace, naive scheduling produces idle time, contention and collision risk; hand-coded allocation rules do not generalise across object layouts.
projects.motivation: Industrial cells increasingly deploy multiple arms for throughput. A reactive, perception-driven allocation policy that is inherently collision-aware is more scalable than rigid, pre-computed schedules.
projects.methodology: A YOLOv8-OBB perception pipeline runs at 30 FPS and feeds a 10 Hz control loop. An improved Artificial Potential Field (iAPF) with exponential attraction and velocity damping resolves inter-arm collisions in real time, while a competitive rule assigns targets by proximity.
projects.technical: Dual Kinova Gen3 Lite arms; oriented-bounding-box detection (YOLOv8-OBB); 30 FPS vision, 10 Hz control; iAPF with exponential attractive potential and velocity damping for stability.
projects.results: Real-time, collision-aware cooperative manipulation with autonomous target assignment, validated on the dual-arm hardware.
projects.future: Learning the allocation policy end-to-end; scaling beyond two arms; tighter coupling between allocation and assembly-level objectives.

projects.title: Improved Artificial Potential Field for Dual-Arm Manipulation
projects.tagline: Real-time inter-arm collision avoidance for asymmetric arms
projects.overview: An improved Artificial Potential Field (iAPF) method that delivers autonomous, collision-aware motion for asymmetric dual-arm manipulators during shared-workspace tasks.
projects.problem: Classical potential fields suffer from local minima and coarse proximity estimates, making them unreliable for close-proximity dual-arm coordination.
projects.motivation: Safe dual-arm operation requires accurate, continuous knowledge of how close the arms are at every instant, computed fast enough to drive reactive control.
projects.methodology: A line-segment-based distance matrix provides precise link-to-link proximity monitoring, integrated with vision-based pose estimation for target detection. Refined potentials produce smooth, collision-free trajectories.
projects.technical: Line-segment distance matrix for proximity; vision-based pose estimation; improved attractive/repulsive potentials; real-time object sorting demonstration.
projects.results: Demonstrated real-time, collision-aware object sorting on a dual-arm system; published in Frontiers in Robotics and AI.
projects.future: Coupling iAPF with learned policies; extension to cluttered, dynamic environments and higher arm counts.

projects.title: Adaptive Policy Blending in Multi-Agent RL for Cooperative Dual-Arm Alignment
projects.tagline: Hierarchical residual MARL with learned coordination blending
projects.overview: A hierarchical residual multi-agent reinforcement-learning framework that interpolates between independent per-arm dexterity and centralised coordination for cooperative dual-arm alignment.
projects.problem: Cooperative dual-arm tasks demand both individual arm skill and tight joint coordination; fixed analytical controllers cannot adapt this balance to the task state.
projects.motivation: Pre-assembly alignment and cooperative picking in industrial automation need policies that generalise beyond hard-coded models while remaining sample-efficient and stable.
projects.methodology: A Centralized Training, Decentralized Execution (CTDE) paradigm combines a pretrained PPO base policy with a MAPPO residual policy. A learned scale-blending parameter (alpha) dynamically interpolates between individual and centralised behaviour, trained with a 92-D global critic and 47-D local observations.
projects.technical: CTDE; PPO base + MAPPO residual; learned blending coefficient alpha; 92-dimensional global critic; 47-dimensional local observations; autonomous target picking and pre-assembly alignment.
projects.results: Enables scalable, generalisable cooperative alignment, offering an adaptive alternative to rigid analytical coordination models.
projects.future: Transfer to physical hardware; extension to multi-stage assembly; generalisation across object geometries and arm morphologies.

projects.title: Vision-Based Bolt Handling and Sorting with a Manipulator
projects.tagline: Deep-learning segmentation plus depth sensing for industrial fasteners
projects.overview: An automated pipeline that identifies, sizes, localises and sorts bolts in unstructured industrial environments using a manipulator.
projects.methodology: Deep-learning segmentation (PPLiteSeg, OCRNet, DeepLabV3+) is combined with classical vision. The segmented binary image is fused with depth from an Intel RealSense D415 to estimate bolt size, position and orientation relative to the robot base.
projects.results: DeepLabV3+ gave the best segmentation, with a mean IoU of 0.95 on a custom dataset covering varied environmental conditions and both new and aged bolts.

projects.title: Dual-Arm Cooperative Manipulation Through Shared Vision
projects.tagline: Classical-vision coordination protocol for two eye-in-hand arms
projects.overview: Two Kinova Gen3 Lite arms with wrist-mounted cameras search a shared workspace and coordinate pick-and-place, with no learned perception or control components.
projects.methodology: Each arm runs ArUco detection on its own camera; the target pose is relayed between base frames via a fixed inter-arm transform, a reachability rule selects the acting arm, and damped least-squares resolved-rate control executes the pick.
projects.results: Validated in Gazebo/ROS2 simulation and on physical dual-arm hardware.

projects.title: Kinematics-Based Real-Time Distance Monitoring for Multi-Arm Safety
projects.tagline: Sensor-free inter-link distance computation for collaborative arms
projects.overview: A geometric, kinematics-based method that computes minimum distances between manipulator links in real time without external sensors.
projects.methodology: Link configurations are classified as parallel, intersecting or skew and reduced to line-segment distances; distance matrices over inter-arm link pairs support systematic collision monitoring.
projects.results: Hardware validation on dual Kinova Gen3 Lite manipulators for inter-arm distance computation in a shared workspace.
